lines: One module carrying the whole Airwindows effect collection, 456 separate stereo effects in this build, one of which runs at a time on the stereo input
Sets one parameter of the chosen effect; the name printed against it, the reading in its tooltip and the span it covers all come from that effect and change when another effect is chosen
Scales the CV input on the same row from -1 to +1 before that CV is added to the parameter knob, and at 0 the CV makes no difference
Scales what both input jacks feed into the effect, 0 to 100 percent, where 100 percent puts a 5V signal into the effect at full scale
Scales what the effect sends to both output jacks, 0 to 100 percent, where 100 percent sends the effect's full scale out as 5V
L input — the left channel into the effect, and with nothing patched to the R input it feeds the right channel too
R input — the right channel into the effect, taken from the L input instead while nothing is patched here
Adds to the parameter knob on the same row after the small knob there scales it; 5V through a fully clockwise scale knob covers that parameter's travel, and the total is clamped to its ends
L output — the left channel out of the effect, at 5V for the effect's full scale
R output — the right channel out of the effect, at 5V for the effect's full scale
Note — the effect is not chosen with a knob. Click the effect name at the top of the panel, or the category above it, for a menu with a search field, a list per category and a collection filter.
Note — the arrows step through the effects in category order and then alphabetically by name, wrapping from the last back to the first, and they ignore the Categories in 'Chris' Order setting.
Note — the question mark at the top of the panel opens Chris Johnson's own text about the chosen effect as an overlay across the module; clicking it again closes it.
Note — the number of parameter knobs follows the chosen effect, between none and ten, and the knobs for parameters that effect does not have are taken off the panel.
Note — the effect works on blocks of samples rather than one sample at a time, four samples by default. A larger block set from the panel menu costs less processor time and delays the sound more.
Note — a new module comes up on Galactic, a reverb, and the arrow on either side of the effect name steps to the next effect without opening a menu.
Note — a CV input stays on the panel, drawn dimmed, when the chosen effect has no parameter on its row, and nothing in the module reads it.
Menu — Panic Reset — builds the chosen effect again from scratch, clearing the delay lines and filter state it is holding, and leaves the knob settings alone
Menu — Monophonic (Sum Inputs) — runs one copy of the effect, adding all the channels at each input jack together into one signal
Menu — Monophonic (MixMaster Sum Input) — runs one copy of the effect, reading each input jack as MixMaster's interleaved left-right pairs and adding those pairs into one stereo signal
Menu — Polyphonic (Stereo to Stereo) — runs a separate copy of the effect on each channel of the input jacks, up to 16 of them, and puts each result on the matching channel of the output jacks
Menu — Polyphonic (MixMaster to MixMaster) — runs a separate copy of the effect on each interleaved left-right pair at the input jacks and writes the results back out as interleaved pairs
Menu — Polyphonic (MixMaster to Stereo) — reads interleaved left-right pairs at the input jacks and sends each pair's result out as its own channel of the L and R outputs
Menu — Polyphonic (Stereo to MixMaster) — reads each channel of the L and R inputs as one stereo pair and writes the results out interleaved
Menu — Block Size — a submenu offering 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64 samples, the first marked 4 (Lowest Latency) and the last 64 (Less CPU); the size in force is printed in the submenu's own name
Menu — Lock Effect Choice — stops the effect being changed, greys out the arrows and disables every effect name in the menus
Menu — Randomize Changes FX Choice — makes Rack's randomize pick a new effect as well as new knob settings, and is overruled by Lock Effect Choice
Menu — Categories in Alphabetical Order — lists the effects inside each category menu by name
Menu — Categories in 'Chris' (quality) Order — lists the effects inside each category menu in the order Chris Johnson gives them in the Airwindopedia, which he arranges by quality rather than by name
Menu — Filter by Collection: Basic, Recommended, Latest, All Effects — on the menu that opens from the effect name: narrows the category lists, the search and the arrows to that collection

Airwin2Rack.notes:
Written against commit d288900, the last commit whose plugin.json carries 2.13.0; the next commit, 03acb46, bumps the version to 2.14.0. Several dozen commits carry 2.13.0, all of them adding effects rather than changing the Rack module, so the installed binary was used to settle which one shipped: PointyDeluxe, PunchyDeluxe and kBeyond are all added in d288900 and all three names are present in plugin.dylib.

Every parameter knob, scale knob and CV jack is described by one line because the module reuses the same ten rows for whatever effect is chosen. What a given row means is set by the effect, not by the panel, which is why no range is quoted for the parameter knobs: the knob is 0 to 1 internally (src-rack/Module.cpp:153) and each effect converts that to its own units and its own printed name (src-rack/Module.cpp:218-228 via getParameterName at :221). The census names the knobs Replace, Brightness, Detune, Bigness and Dry/Wet because those are Galactic's parameter names and a fresh module comes up on Galactic (src-rack/Module.cpp:162).

Parameters 10 and 21 are declared, named Unused, and given no widget (src-rack/Module.cpp:83-89 and :142-143), so neither can be clicked and neither gets a line. They are placeholders kept so that older patches still load.

CV inputs 10 and 11 exist as jacks but no effect has more than ten parameters, and the CV loop is bounded by that count, so the last two jacks are never read. The maker names them Unused CV.

The manual says the module holds 300 or more effects; the shipped build registers 456 of them (src/ModuleAdd.h at d288900). The manual also says the ordering setting applies to the menus, which is right for the Rack module: the arrow buttons always walk the alphabetical-within-category order (src-rack/Module.cpp:1058 calling AirwinRegistry::neighborIndexFor), and only the JUCE build's jog buttons follow the Chris order.

The effect selector, the arrow buttons and the question mark are plain widgets rather than parameters, so none of them can be clicked for help; they are covered by Note lines instead. The Light Mode and Dark Mode menu items are left out as cosmetic.
